Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I’m attaching a concise activation matrix that lays out three reservation paths we recommend based on your forecasted inference mix (chat-heavy + embedding batch jobs). The goal: give you predictable baseline throughput while preserving short-term surge capacity during product launches.

High level summary (attachment: Sundial_Reservation_Matrix_v2.xlsx):
- Option A (Conservative): 24 GPUs baseline, 48 GPU burst, 30-day ramp to full traffic. Minimal cost, slower warm-up.
- Option B (Balanced): 48 GPUs baseline, 96 GPU burst, 14-day staged ramp with a 7-day canary. Recommended for production launch.
- Option C (Aggressive): 96 GPUs baseline, 160 GPU burst, 7-day ramp. For high-concurrency beta and heavy embeddings.

Key guardrails we suggest:
- Min-GPU floor: keep 20% of baseline pinned to ensure cold-starts don’t impact SLAs.
- Canary: 7-day canary with 10% traffic on a dedicated lane.
- Surge policy: automated burst to reserved pool + regional fallback to secondary region if average tail latency > 350ms.

Open items I flagged in the matrix for your input: preferred canary length, whether you need cross-region replication for the initial launch, and any procurement timing constraints.

Attached: Sundial_Reservation_Matrix_v2.xlsx; I also dropped a short slide deck with the ramp visual (Sundial_Ramp_SLA_Slides.pdf).

If this looks directionally correct I’ll loop in Grace from Onboarding and Nikhil from Infra to align the warm-start plan and activation windows.

Thanks —
Chloe Martin

Emma —

Thanks — below are the clarifications and a short line-item quote. I’ve also attached a versioned quote (Sundial_Quote_v3.pdf) to speed procurement.

Operational detail: Min-GPU floor and billing
- Baseline reservation = GPUs you commit to (you pay for these as reserved capacity).
- Min-GPU floor = we recommend reserving an additional 20% of baseline pinned (not opportunistic) as a warm pool. This reduces tail latency spikes during autoscaling. Example: Balanced baseline 48 GPUs -> recommended pinned warm pool = 9 GPUs (20% -> round up to 10). You pay reserved rates for baseline + pinned warm pool.
- Burst buffer (up to the burst limit) is metered at a lower overage price while reserved capacity is saturated. We list both reserved and burst rates in the attached quote.

Canary gating metrics (we use these for rollback/advance):
- 95th percentile latency stable and < 350ms for generator requests
- Error rate < 0.5% (inferred model errors + infra errors)
- Token throughput >= 85% of expected baseline for the canary traffic slice

Cross-region failover cost & accounting:
- Cross-region standby (hot-standby) is an additional flat fee + 30% of baseline reserved price (covers replication and reserved throughput).
- In failover, traffic served from standby will be billed as part of your burst credits up to the burst limit; beyond that this will be charged as on-demand usage.

Suggested activation timeline (we recommend starting onboarding 4 weeks pre-launch):
- T-28 to T-21: Provision baseline GPUs + warm pool, initial infra validation (internal testing).
- T-21 to T-14: 7d canary on 10% traffic. Gate by metrics above.
- T-14 to T-7: Gradual ramp to 50% traffic (staged autoscaling profiles).
- T-7 to T0: Ramp to 100% and enable burst policy for launch windows.

Line-item quote (summary from Sundial_Quote_v3.pdf):
- Baseline reserved (Balanced): 48x A100-80GB equiv - monthly reserved fee: $XXX,XXX
- Pinned warm pool (20%): 10x - monthly reserved fee: $XX,XXX
- Burst buffer (up to 96 total): overage rate $Y/token-equivalent; capped monthly at $ZZ,ZZZ for planning
- Cross-region standby: flat fee $AA,AAA + 30% of baseline reserved cost
- Onboarding & canary support (one-time): $BB,BBB (includes 2 weeks of SRE on-call and runbook validation)

Attachments: Sundial_Quote_v3.pdf (application/pdf)
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/SNDL-2028-07; https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/sundial-reservation-2028
